target_customer: Product, engineering and design teams at fast-moving Series A and B software startups
problem: Dashboards show numbers but not why users stay, leave or pay; watching session replays by hand does not scale. Human Behavior uses vision models to watch every session and turn the findings into actions.
product_category: AI product analytics and session replay analysis

founders.name: Amogh Chaturvedi
education: Stanford, computer science (dropped out, per TechCrunch)
previous_startups: Dough, bootstrapped e-commerce accounting tool, sold for six figures to Employer.com (per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: Organized a hacker house in 2023 where the three founders met. YC page says VLM research at Stanford NLP Group.

founders.name: Chirag Kawediya
education: UChicago, computer science (per YC page; TechCrunch says college graduate)
founders.background_notes: YC page mentions UChicago Database Group research.

founders.name: Skyler Ji
education: UC Berkeley, computer science (dropped out, per TechCrunch)

competitors.name: PostHog
competitors.what: Product analytics with session replay, later added an AI replay analysis agent (Replay Vision)

competitors.name: Contentsquare, Quantum Metric, FullStory, LogRocket
competitors.what: Session replay vendors adding AI summaries
competitors.traction_then: enterprise incumbents; exact launch dates not established

technical_complexity.rationale: Applies vision-language models to recorded sessions at scale; founders cite VLM research. Standard SaaS engineering plus cost-sensitive model pipelines.

defensibility.rationale: Incumbent replay and analytics vendors could add the same AI analysis layer, and PostHog shipped an AI replay agent. Moat would depend on speed and integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents shipped AI session analysis features during 2025 and 2026; no acquisition of Human Behavior found.

market_need_then: Teams already spend on analytics and replay tools, and complain that dashboards do not explain why users behave as they do. Cheaper vision models in 2025 made automated replay review practical.

identity.mascot_or_character: hand-drawn avatar illustrations on the site
identity.visual_style: playful illustrated avatars, remixed CC BY 4.0 art
identity.voice_and_tone: bold and punchy, for example 'Dashboards are where insights go to die'

branding.brand_signature: punchy anti-dashboard copy and illustrated avatars
branding.community_and_virality: Has a Discord community. Fundraise story drew wide press for founders aged 20 and 22.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic descriptive name that is hard to search for, offset by lively site voice and strong launch press.

pivots.why: Per TechCrunch the founders pivoted and sold Dough; reasons not detailed.

outcome_analysis: Human Behavior raised a $5M seed in September 2025 within two days, helped by cheap vision models and a young repeat-founder team with a prior small exit. It is early and active. The main risk is that incumbents such as PostHog already ship AI replay analysis, so durability depends on execution speed.
notes: Searches found no shutdown, acquisition or layoffs. TechCrunch lead investor is unclear; one search summary said Accel and RTP Global co-led, which conflicts with other outlets and is unverified. A StartupIntros entry of $500K in 2025-06 is unverified. Competitor dates are approximate (2025 era comparison pages); PostHog Replay Vision date not established.
